question: A shopkeeper sold two articles for ₹560 each. He incurred no loss and made no profit in the transaction because one article was sold at a loss of 16(2)/(3)% and the other article was sold at a profit of:
solution:
Given:

Selling price of each article = ₹560

Loss incurred on selling one article = 16(2)/(3)% = 50/3 %

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article that is sold at loss be Q.

According to the question,

Q - Q × 50/3 % = 560

⇒ Q - Q/6 = 560

⇒ 5Q/6 = 560

⇒ Q/6 = 112

⇒ Q = 112 × 6

⇒ Q = 672

Let the cost price of the other article be R that is sold is G% profit.

According to the question,

R + 672 = 560 × 2

⇒ R = 1120 - 672

⇒ R = 448

The cost price of the other article = ₹448

According to the question,

448 + 448 × G% = 560

⇒ 448 (1 + G/100) = 560

⇒ (1 + G/100) = 560/448

⇒ (1 + G/100) = 1.25

⇒ G/100 = 1.25 - 1

⇒ G/100 = 0.25

⇒ G = 25

**∴ The other article was sold at a profit of 25%.**
